utterances.text: But wait for my question, please. Do you recall any other guard who in particular abused detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: I think that he stood out in particular. Dragomir or Mihajlo Vukovic. I'm not actually sure about the first name. But I wouldn't want Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to mix him up with Manojlo Vukovic, who was dark, somewhat older than the previously-mentioned person, and he was pretty moderate. He was a police officer before, and I knew him from KP Dom. The first-mentioned person was young, had brown hair, tall, and he -- it was characteristic of him when the group that was taken out on the 17th of September, 1993, 45 of them, that he at that time had disappeared so that he didn't appear in the camp for some six months, which was quite suspicious in view of the disappearance of these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Witness, I had asked you if besides Burilo, is there anyone you remember among the guards who abused detainees so that you saw it actually.

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: No. This was hidden from view. They were officials simply. I didn't really see anybody in particular abusing anybody else. Perhaps there would be a slap or something, but this would be done in a tempter. But this was also something that didn't happen so often. So I didn't see that the police particularly abused those -- at least those who had direct contact with us, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were detained in the KP Dom until the 5th of July, 1993. Where were you taken then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes. I was taken to the Kula camp near Sarajevo, not far from the airport. That's also an area that was previously used as a corrections centre, just like KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long were you detained there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: I was there until I was exchanged on June 15, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many detainees were detained in Kula; do you know?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: I think there were about 80 to 100 people, and it was a constant figure because some people would come, some people would escape, others were brought in. So there was a constant change in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when we speak about 80 to 100 people, were they all of one ethnic group or were there different ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: They were mostly Bosniaks and two or three Croats who were with us directly, but it did happen that a military unit surrendered to the Serbs at Grbavica, 67 of them. So the Serbs brought them to the camp. So these 67 Croats were held separately. So separately from us, the 80 to 100 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were the conditions in Kula compared to KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: They were the same. We were placed on the ground floor, so it was used as a camp for a year or more. There was a lot of damp. It was messy. There was no heat. Conditions were bad. The hygienic conditions were bad. There were lice again and other problems there as well. I would also like to mention a group, a larger group of mentally-ill patients who were captured around the Sarajevo front lines, and the Serbs managed to get their soldiers in exchange, and they were -- these people were mentally-ill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did people disappear from this camp as well while you were detained there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Not in such large numbers. They were not taken out for execution in such large numbers, if I may say, but they disappeared in other ways. It would happen that they would go to a work location and then they would be killed, and it would be staged as if they had gotten killed by their own side on the separation line, or they would come across a minefield and so on. So this is how people were frequently seriously wounded and they were killed. There were several cases where they were so seriously wounded. There was the case of one young man who died because he suddenly got diabetes. He was a craftsman, and he maintained the -- some sort of facility. He was from Grapska, close to Doboj, and he had gone through a few camps by that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how do you know that detainees disappeared from Kula as well? Did you actually see it or did you hear anything about it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I saw it personally. They would go to a work location in the morning and then they would be gone. There was a case where they would be perhaps seriously wounded. They would go to the hospital; they would die there. Then detainees would go to bury them. They would also go to bury Serbs or to transfer Serbs to another grave. There were difference tasks that were performed by the detainees. This happened -- I mean, these contrived murders would happen on Christmas. In January 1993, at early morning hours, at 5.00 perhaps, five or six people were taken away, and then on the separation line, two of them were killed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said January 1993. That's probably a mistake then, according to --

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I'm sorry. I meant 1994. It was a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. We do not need to go into more details of the Kula camp. I just want to show you now two documents. The first document is the document identification number 209. When you look at it, is it -- does it confirm your time of detention in Foca and Kula?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: No. It confirms the total time I was detained in Foca and Kula, from the 15th -- until the 15th of June, 1994. So this is true. This is the true date.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The Prosecution would like to enter this document as Prosecution Exhibit 209. It's a certificate from the commission of the location of missing persons of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Does it have a starting date?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. It is from the 11th November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in addition, we would like to have the witness shown the item number 210 of the trial binders. It's a certificate from the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: They will need to be under seal, will they?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, both. We would like to enter this into evidence as well. It's a certificate from the Red Cross, although it shows different dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He explained that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, he explained that already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection to this, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. These will be Exhibits P209 and P210. Each of them will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you need not bother with this document any longer. You have already explained why there are different dates on it. Witness, you have mentioned to us the injuries and physical results of the detention that you sustained, and you spoke about the fear you had. Did this cause any permanent physical or mental results on your health?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes. I already mentioned that several times. Because of the long-term poor food that we received, I lost a lot of weight. I had difficulties moving. I had an inflammation of the nerves in the right leg. So I had problems in walking because of that inflammation. I had swellings on my legs as a result of poor nutrition. My vision is weak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let me interrupt you. I was asking if you still have -- if you have permanent results. That means do you still suffer nowadays any physical or mental problems?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Unfortunately, all of these things that I have mentioned are still there today, perhaps in a milder form, meaning the symptoms, because today I get tired very easily in my extremities. So after six hours of work, I get very tired. Before I would work 12 to 16 hours and I wouldn't feel tired. I was in very good physical shape. I don't smoke. I don't drink. I was very careful. I am very careful about my psychological and physical condition because I have had obligations also in my work and my family. But today, all of these duties are very much reduced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you still suffer mentally today and, if so, in which way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes. The main psychological consequence is chronic sleeplessness, insomnia. Today I can't sleep without medication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are the questions of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to introduce myself to the witness. Cross-examined by Mr. Bakrac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is lawyer Mihajlo Bakrac. I represent the accused Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I ask the question, I would like to say good day to you.

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said that you were a member of the Democratic Action Party.

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But not a leader.

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: That I never -- when I went to the party and when I joined the party, I never intended to become one of the leading figures in the party. I was -- the leaders would always worry me and they would get on my nerves if in any of their -- whatever they did or said they would disrupt relations between the ethnic groups. So in this sense, I meant that I didn't want to be a leader nor was I a leader. And the others annoyed me and worried me when they would emphasise this too much in their public appearances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a moment. Sir, when you are speaking the same language as --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sorry. When you are speaking the same language as the person examining you, you should wait until the translators have caught up with the question before you start the answer. If you just give a short pause before you answer, then the translators will be able to catch up. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: I apologise, Presiding Judge. You warned me about this a few times already, but it happens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is the first time that it has happened when you're being cross-examined by somebody speaking the same language, and it's accentuated there. So that's why I've drawn it to your attention again. So pause slightly to allow the translators to catch up. Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before we continue, could I ask the witness to turn towards the person who is asking the questions, because it's difficult to follow the answers if the witness is turned towards the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't think that we can tell him to do anything like that, Mr. Bakrac. You can hear him just as well as you heard him Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. when he was answering the Prosecution, if I may say so. I know why you've asked for that, but I don't think it would be appropriate to ask the witness to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Then I will try to proceed and put my questions in this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever, as a member of the Democratic Action Party, run for any post?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted). I didn't have any particular desire to do this, but this was suggested by the party and this passed. I did lose in these elections. I did lose to my rival. I never regretted this because I always knew that I was doing a job. I was in a profession which I would never change for a different one, particularly not for any kind of political function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if I understand you rightly, you didn't refuse this nomination.

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes, this is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to tell me whether the Democratic Action Party was a national, purely national party?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes, just as SDS was in Foca. Yes. Mostly it was a national party, but all the membership really did try not to have -- tried to prevent any nationalism from appearing in the party, which made a difference. The aim of the party was to foster neighbourly relations towards its neighbours. So I had nothing against the Serbs having some kind of party which would unite them. I just want to say that there were other parties at the local elections in 1990 where there were Bosniaks. We will mention NBO, the Reformist Party, and also the former communists which also had a majority of Bosniaks for its members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the Serb ethnic group didn't have any other party other than SDS?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, they didn't have any other party. But this does not mean that any of the Serbs could not join any of the parties that I mentioned, particularly the Reformist or the Communist Party in the local elections in 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were a member of the Democratic Action Party, could you please tell us which of those two parties, I mean the SDA and the Serbian Democratic Party, could you please tell us which of those parties was founded first in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: I really can't remember which one of them was established first. I know that the SDA was established sometime in May in 1990. I've already talked about the party platform, what the party stood for in its declarations and what its goals were: unified military, foreign policy, and also joint currency, a common currency. We had no idea about what would happen later, these conflicts between people. This was such a far-off thing. If this was something that we could predict, I would never have joined such a party if we had any idea if there would be divisions and disagreements between these people. When the party was founded and all the other parties, and their programmes were something that was appropriate for everybody, and we were talking about parliamentary election and the seats that they would win according to the number of votes they won and according to the population. But it was true that Serbs usually had more power, even in municipalities where the majority was comprised by the Bosniak population. Sir, you are from Serbia, but it's a fact that this was the way things were in Bosnia. Even though in some municipalities Serbs were in a minority, they would have more power, and I think that the multiparty system was something that didn't suit them because they had concluded that based on that system, they wouldn't have as much authority as they had before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, could I -- was this something that bothered you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: No. No. This is a conclusion that we got to later from the context of everything that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, especially when the answers are so long, you really must pause before the next question. The witness is having trouble, but you should be used to it by now. And the longer the answer, the longer it takes for the translator to catch up. You've been very good, but that one was not good.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please tell me which party of these two national parties first organised a rally in the region of Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: You mean a promotional meeting. The SDA held its meeting first. It was provided -- there was no attempt to rush into it. A few days later, the Serbian Democratic Party had such a meeting because they had their own programme. Nobody influenced anybody else. At that time there were promotional gatherings being held throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what nationality was the first victim in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: You're thinking of these conflicts that will happen later, that will come later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, after the foundation of the national parties. The first victim shortly before the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know the nationality of -- people started to get killed, so who was the first, I really can't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will try to remind you. This is an incident in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes. I know that quite early on, a young Bosniak was killed not far from a place called Kobilja Glava. Whether he was killed before the first or whether there was some incident before in the town close to the Orthodox church perhaps, but I really can't remember what happened before, if that's what you're thinking of. And I don't know why that would be significant in the context of everything here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask you not to think about the significance of my question. If you can answer, that's fine, but did I understand rightly that you remember that the first incident took place at the Orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes. You reminded me, and I have given you the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell me roughly how many people attended the SDA rally in Foca and were you present there? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Yes, I was present there, and I'm not sure exactly. There were different estimates. Perhaps around 100.000 people or something like that. There were many Serbs present there as officials, and also citizens could attend. I saw a lot of my colleagues there. They were listening to the talks and everything. Mr. Ostojic was a guest from the Serbian Democratic Party as a person from Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me after that where the rally of the Serbian Democratic Party was held and do you know perhaps how many people attended that rally?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: It was held at the Sutjeska stadium, but I really don't know how many people attended. I don't know any specifics. I stated before that I had some family business and I was away from Foca at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some witnesses here mentioned that the number of people there was 10.000 people. Did you hear something like that and can you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: Well, I have stated already what I know, so I don't want to repeat that. Everybody has their own opinion and also their idea of how many people were present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell me roughly at that time how many -- at the time these rallies were held what the population was of the town of Foca and the municipality of Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-111
utterances.text: The municipality of Foca had a population. The inner city region had about 13.000 people, and the municipality of Foca had a population of 22.000. In percentages, I think this would be 52 per cent Bosniaks, 48 per cent Serbs and Montenegrins, so counting the 3 per cent of Montenegrins there, and also 2 per cent of others. So I think these are the rough percentages.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think this is perhaps an appropriate time to close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume at 9.30 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
